text: From the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Name two items that were always available to Alex the parrot without him having to request
them.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one methodological weakness of this study.

text: From the study by Pepperberg (parrot learning):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
One feature of the sample in this study was that they were all adults.
Identify three other features of the sample used in this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one result about dream recall from REM awakenings in the first half of the night
compared to the second half of the night.

text: From the study by Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreams):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
At the end of the study by Milgram (obedience), the experimenter used an ‘interview and
dehoax’ procedure with his participants.
Describe this procedure.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Studies in social psychology can be used to help managers in the workplace.
Suggest how the study by Milgram could be used to help a manager with disobedient workers.
Your suggestion must be ethical.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline one aim of this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one reason why the procedure was standardised in this study.

text: From the study by Canli et al. (brain scans and emotions):
Outline what is meant by the ‘learning approach’ in psychology. Include examples from the study
by Saavedra and Silverman (button phobia) in your answer.
From the study by Laney et al. (false memory):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline the category of ‘initiates new activity’ for the behaviour of participants in the Euphoria
condition.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two friends, Maryam and Zara, are discussing this study in terms of reliability.
Maryam believes the study does have reliability but Zara believes the study does not have
reliability.
Outline why you think either Maryam or Zara is correct, using evidence from the study.
